text.card: Widen and narrow a real polygonal opening with three original coupled blades.
text.wrong_phase: Choose the neighboring setting matching the current phase; the wide and narrow ends do not wrap.
text.free_hand: Free a hand to turn the iris ring rim.
text.howto_turn: Use a free hand on the right-hand ring rim to narrow or widen this mounted three-blade iris one indexed setting at a time. The white ring index and W and N references mark the wide and narrow ends. The same three colored rigid blades pivot on their fixed original axes; each original drive stud travels inside a genuine open radial channel in the same adjusting ring. Continuous axles, hollow receiver bores, rear collars and retaining heads keep the original blades and ring captured on the connected frame. The through-opening is formed by the actual union of the three straight inner edges inside the fixed open mask. Its projected area decreases through eight settings from about144132 to26021 square millimetres, remains open at the narrow end and widens back without a wrap or reset. It is a polygonal aperture, not a circular camera diaphragm. Nominal300 millimetre pivot radius and rigid120 millimetre stud spacing give alpha=phi+asin(2.5sin(phi)); the ring ranges from0 to15 degrees, with whole-millidegree tables and rounded fixed pivots retaining positive geometric clearances. Each whole blade rotates by120*j+alpha about its own fixed pivot; no member scales or changes its original vertices. Inspect the assembled layers from an oblique view. Stored pictures select endpoints: a separately verified analytic geometric path does not imply interpolated browser motion, physical force or friction, a motion solver, elastic blade contact, a mechanical hardstop, complete closure, nested screen regions, light or exposure simulation, optical performance, photography, or loose-item custody.
